title: The Last Number Is the Answer

steps.body: Counting's biggest secret: the last number said is not just the last toy's name — it tells how many are in the WHOLE group.
steps.narration: Counting's biggest secret: the last number said is not just the last toy's name — it tells how many are in the WHOLE group.

widget.prompt: Count 5 shells, then show the group's number with counters.

commonCounts.feedback: One names only the final shell; the question asks about the whole group.
The count did not stop at 4 — one more shell took the count to 5.

widget.missFeedback: Count the shells one by one; the number you end on is the group's number.
widget.successFeedback: Five — the last word of the count names the whole group at once.

predict.reveal: The final count word answers “how many” for everything counted, not for one shell.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch cardinality.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch cardinality.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: After counting “1, 2, 3, 4, 5”, what does the 5 tell you?

options.label: How many there are in the whole group
options.feedback: Correct — the last number names the size of the whole group, not just one object.

options.label: The name of the last toy only
options.feedback: The 5 belongs to the group; the last toy is simply where the count finished.

options.label: That the toys are big
options.feedback: Counting measures how many, never how large.

options.label: That you must count again
options.feedback: One careful count is enough — its last number IS the answer.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 12? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 12 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 13.
14 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 12 lands on 13.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 12 and count on 1: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: 13 — one hop forward, because each number is exactly one more than the last.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 13.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 12 means one hop, stopping on 13.
